headline: High-risk shared filesystem and unsandboxed flow execution create dangerous default interaction between Continue and Langflow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue reads and writes workspace files and uses MCP; Langflow can ingest uploaded files and chain tools in flows. That creates a plausible instruction-injection path through shared files or flow inputs. The pair is not documented as isolated, so the interaction is more than manual copy-paste, but not clearly a raw-web parser case.
conditions: IF Langflow flow inputs include files or text produced by Continue without sanitization
IF Continue reads a workspace file that Langflow later treats as instructions
mitigations: Add a strict delimiter and provenance tag to all cross-agent text
Disable file-based handoff between the tools
Require human review before Langflow executes any instruction-like content
Use separate workspaces for each agent
requires-engineering: add content filtering or prompt-firewalling at the integration boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code and open editor buffers, while Langflow reads server filesystem and uploaded flow files. Both have broad network egress and can send content to model providers or HTTP services. Shared filesystem/state makes leakage plausible in default setups, though the profiles do not prove uncontrolled third-party exfiltration.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or uploaded files
IF either agent forwards file contents to a remote model provider or HTTP service
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials per agent
Restrict Langflow flows from reading source-code directories
Turn off uploads for sensitive files
Use local-only model providers for both agents
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue has filesystem write access and shared state via filesystem across instances; Langflow has filesystem write access plus server-side state and unsandboxed Python code by default. If both operate on the same directory or shared mutable resources, concurrent writes can corrupt files or overwrite each other's outputs. The default overlap is dangerous and not lock-protected in the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or shared store
IF Langflow Python components mutate files that Continue also edits
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories to each agent
Disable Langflow file-writing components for shared paths
Pause one agent while the other writes
Use OS-level file locks on shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can produce code or instructions from editor context, and Langflow can chain agents and tools in flows. If Langflow consumes Continue's output as authoritative, errors can cascade into automated actions or downstream tool calls. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary, so the safer reading is that default flow composition can amplify mistakes.
conditions: IF Langflow uses Continue-generated text as a flow input without verification
IF a Langflow node triggers tools or actions based on that text
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any downstream action
Require citations or structured schemas from Continue outputs
Mark Continue output as untrusted in Langflow
Limit Langflow nodes to read-only evaluation
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Continue handles model-provider API keys and workspace code, while Langflow stores per-flow credentials and processes uploaded files/server filesystem data. The profiles show different storage and retention surfaces, so compliance risk exists if regulated data is routed through both. No specific residency or certification mismatch is proven, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into both agents' workspaces or flows
IF Langflow stores credentials or outputs longer than Continue's editor-session context
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared flows
Use separate retention policies for each agent
Disable logging of sensitive prompts and outputs
Review credential storage settings in Langflow
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both systems
